summary: Gifford Pinchot NF summit with east and west lookout sites (1922-1960); the 1946 two-story cab was moved in 2005, and a replica top story stands in Entiat.

facts.design: prototype two-story 14 by 14 foot frame cab, 1946; the only one of its style
facts.status_note: The 1946 east cab was dismantled and moved in 2005 per FFLOS and FireLookout.com. WillhiteWeb says a replica of its top story now stands at Columbia Breaks in Entiat. The west house was destroyed in 1960.

access.note: Drive-up on forest roads (FR 8821) with a rocky last mile, per WillhiteWeb

visit.trail_note: The west side needs a walk because deadfall blocks the old route, per WillhiteWeb

events.note: 16 by 20 foot frame house on the east end. WillhiteWeb says 1922; FFLOS says about 1921
Amos Pearce of nearby White Salmon, per WillhiteWeb
House moved to the west end of the summit
7 by 7 foot frame cab built on the east end; FFLOS says about this time
Darrel and Zoa Couch of Trout Lake were lookouts in 1932 and for a few years after
7 by 7 foot cab replaced by an L-5 cab
Two screened porches and an observation cupola added to the west house
Myron Halse stationed at the lookout
Prototype two-story 14 by 14 foot cab with slanted windows and a curved hip roof, on the east end
Mr. and Mrs. Ernest Fiedler, then Forest Couch for the rest of the season
Cabin on the west side (the house) destroyed
Klickitat County PUD strung power lines from the Trout Lake area to the summit
East cab dismantled by the FFLA and relocated to the Columbia Breaks Fire Interpretive Center in Entiat
Registered June 23, 2012, nominated by Ray Kresek

corrections.why: The 1946 east cab was dismantled and moved in 2005 per FFLOS, and WillhiteWeb describes a replica of its top story at Columbia Breaks in Entiat. Gone describes only the summit and the west house, which was destroyed in 1960.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS says about 1921 for the first frame house; WillhiteWeb says 1922. Not resolved; the story gives both.

FFLOS and FireLookout.com say the east cab was dismantled and relocated in 2005. WillhiteWeb says Columbia Breaks built a replica of the top story, reusing some old wood. Not resolved; the story gives both accounts.
The Columbia Breaks history page says Highway 97A; the WillhiteWeb center page says US Highway 97 about a mile north of Entiat. The story gives only the town and the page's highway.

notes_for_editor: The brief's status 'gone' is corrected to relocated: the east cab was moved in 2005, and WillhiteWeb describes a replica of its top story at Columbia Breaks. The register and WillhiteWeb disagree on whether the Columbia Breaks structure is the original cab or a replica; the story reports both. Agency is U.S. Forest Service per the register, with the land in the Gifford Pinchot NF; the register also calls DNR the landowner, which the story repeats. Access is drive-up per WillhiteWeb; no closure is mentioned in the sources read. The Columbia Breaks center's current opening hours were not checked. Reads: 5 pages (one re-read for the 'Location Today' text), 2 searches.
